title: A closed adopt session's in-flight round keeps running model legs
body:
## Summary
When an adopt session is closed (DELETE, idle expiry, shutdown) mid-round, the round already on its actor keeps calling legs: the parallel audit, the brief leg and the interview retry all run to completion as cold `claude -p` calls whose answers nobody can read.

## Description
AdoptSession.close() sets `cancelled` and shuts the actor down with `cancel_futures=True` (src/athena/adopt/session.py:456-464), which cancels only rounds not yet started. The running round in src/athena/adopt/loop.py never reads `session.cancelled`: `_after_answers` (loop.py:278-296) runs `_both(audit, interview)`, then `_write_brief` runs the audit-tier brief leg (loop.py:465-477), and `_offer` may run a retry interview (loop.py:388). The warm interviewer is now cancelled at close (commit a262a8e6), but the cold legs are not, and every one is a billed invocation ledgered under a conversation that is gone. Registry: durable-agent-operations / two-cancellations-and-a-synchronous-door (an effect must not start after cancellation was requested). Fixed looks like: `session.run_leg` refuses (answers a `cancelled` LegResult, ledgered as such or not at all) once `session.cancelled` is set, and the loop returns at its next step.

## Flow
- POST /adopt, answer the first card -> the actor runs _after_answers: audit and interview legs start in parallel
- DELETE /adopt/<sid> while they run -> close() cancels the warm interviewer and the queued futures
- the audit leg (cold) finishes; _write_brief or _offer_card then starts another cold leg on the closed session
- build order: a cancellation check in AdoptSession.run_leg (answer cancelled, no transport call), then early returns in loop._after_answers/_write_brief

## Expected impact
The person pays nothing for a session they closed; spend after close stops being possible. Measured by counting transport calls started after close. Could break: a lane or showcase leg that legitimately finishes after close (they already stop on `cancelled`).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no model leg starts after the session was closed
Before: walked: a close during `_after_answers` leaves 1-3 cold legs to start after close (the brief leg and the retry interview are started after the parallel pair returns)
After: 0 legs started after close
Method: simulation - three cases walked (close during the parallel pair; during the brief leg; during the retry); a red test needs a slow fake transport that blocks per call, which this round did not build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/adopt/session.py:456-464 close(): cancelled.set(); _actor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
src/athena/adopt/loop.py:287-296 _after_answers runs _both(audit, interview) then _write_brief / _offer_card with no cancelled check
src/athena/adopt/session.py:350-382 run_leg forwards to LegRunner.run_leg unconditionally
grep -n cancelled src/athena/adopt/loop.py -> no match
instrument: tests/adopt: a FakeTransport whose run() blocks on an Event per call; close the session while the first leg blocks, release it, drain, and count transport.requests started after close (control red: >=1 today)

title: Approving the same rev twice in one session writes two approvals and two episodes
body:
## Summary
A second POST /adopt/<sid>/approve with the rev already approved in this session is accepted and writes the case again: a second approval row for the same rev, a second approval episode, and the confirmed slots' facts re-written.

## Description
loop.approve (src/athena/adopt/loop.py:157-170) refuses only a stale or wrong rev; it never looks at `session.approved_rev`. routes.approve (src/athena/adopt/routes.py:429-455) then calls CaseBook.save every time, and save (src/athena/adopt/cases.py:332-443) appends an episode, writes a fact per confirmed `user` slot and appends a CaseApproval. A double-click, a retried request after a dropped reply, or the desktop resending is two approvals of one shown draft. The showcase is already guarded (`showcase_again`, src/athena/adopt/showcase.py:648-654); the case file is not. Note the legitimate case that must survive: a reopened case approved again at its unchanged rev is a NEW approval (tests/adopt/test_cases.py, [1, 1]) - the guard is per session, not per rev.

## Flow
- start, answer, POST approve {rev: 1} -> case saved, approvals [1]
- POST approve {rev: 1} again in the same session -> 200, approvals [1, 1], a second episode, facts rewritten
- build order: record the saved rev on the session (e.g. session.saved_rev) under case_lock; save() of a rev this session already saved answers the case unchanged

## Expected impact
The case file's approval history and the brain's episodes say what the person actually did, once. Measured by approvals length after two identical POSTs. Could break: a client that relies on re-approve rewriting the file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one approval per shown draft per session
Before: two identical approve POSTs in one session -> 2 approval rows, 2 episodes (walked through cases.py:372-428)
After: 1 approval row, 1 episode; the second POST answers the same case_id
Method: simulation - walked the route and save(); the route test that would prove it was not written this round because the right behaviour for a retried request (200 with the same case vs 409) is a product choice
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/adopt/loop.py:157-170 approve(): only stale/current-rev checks
src/athena/adopt/routes.py:445-455 book.save(session, rev) on every accepted approve
src/athena/adopt/cases.py:372 append_episode; :384 write_fact; :428 approvals=(*prior.approvals, approval)
instrument: tests/adopt/test_cases.py: approve_one(), then POST approve {rev: 1} again on the same session; assert len(approvals) == 1 and one approval episode (control red: 2 today)

title: Brief writer and setup lines disagree on a reopened guessed slot
body:
## Summary
A slot a reopened case turned back into a guess (status guessed, source memory) is told to the brief writer as "you said it, in your earlier case" while the mechanical setup lines and the command mark it "(my guess)".

## Description
prompts._origin (src/athena/adopt/prompts.py:335-342) maps a non-confirmed slot to "Athena's guess" only for source default/user, so guessed+memory falls through to _ORIGIN['memory'] = "you said it, in your earlier case" - and BRIEF_SYSTEM says her words carry no mark. slots.provenance (src/athena/adopt/slots.py:362-376) gives guessed+memory " (my guess)", the mark reserved for Athena's own inference. So the model-written brief prints a reopened date bare (as her current word) while the fallback setup lines call her own earlier words Athena's guess; neither says what it is: her earlier word, now unconfirmed. Two renderings of one rule (ADR 0123 reopening, UAT 2026-10-23 theme 3 honest marks).

## Flow
- approve a case with a dated fact confirmed -> restart -> reopen: the fact is guessed/memory
- answer nothing and press enough: the brief prompt row reads '[fact, guessed, you said it, in your earlier case]' (no mark) while _setup_lines reads '... (my guess)'
- build order: one table (status x source -> mark) both modules read, with a mark for 'your earlier answer, to check' agreed by the owner

## Expected impact
The brief never states a may-have-moved date as current, and never calls her own words Athena's guess. Measured by a status x source table test over both renderings. Could break: the brief-honesty bench lines that pin today's marks.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - both renderings classify every (status, source) pair alike
Before: 1 of 18 (status x source) pairs disagree: guessed+memory ('you said it' vs '(my guess)'); found by reading both tables
After: 0 of 18 disagree
Method: probe - the two functions read side by side over the 18 pairs; not built because the new mark's wording is the owner's (UAT theme 3)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/adopt/prompts.py:338-342 if slot.status != 'confirmed' and slot.source in ('default', 'user'): return ", Athena's guess"; else _ORIGIN[source]
src/athena/adopt/slots.py:370-376 confirmed->...; source in _FROM -> from ...; else ' (my guess)'  (memory not in _FROM)
src/athena/adopt/cases.py:263-264 reopen: confirmed+perishable -> guessed, source memory
instrument: tests/adopt/test_brief_honesty.py: parametrize all 3 statuses x 6 sources; assert prompts._origin and slots.provenance put each pair in the same class (her words / playbook / lane / guess / earlier-answer)

title: A 401 sent before the body is read aborts the client socket on Windows
body:
## Summary
tests/adopt/test_routes.py::test_every_route_wants_the_token failed once this round with WinError 10053 (connection aborted) instead of reading the 401: the daemon answers a tokenless POST without reading its body and closes, and Windows resets the socket under the unread bytes.

## Description
The daemon's refusal path (src/athena/daemon/server.py:809 and :939 `_fail(error(401, 'foreign_token', ...))`, `Connection: close`) replies before the request body is consumed. A client that has sent `{}` and then reads gets a RST on Windows when the server closes with unread input, so the 401 is lost: in tests a flake (1 of 9 runs of the scoped suite this round; 3/3 green alone), in production a desktop that shows 'connection aborted' where 'the token is wrong' was sent. Out of this round's paths (daemon-service owns server.py).

## Flow
- POST /adopt with a body and no token
- server: token check fails -> 401 written -> socket closed with the body unread
- client: recv -> WinError 10053 instead of the 401
- build order: drain (or read up to the declared Content-Length, bounded) before any refusal that closes

## Expected impact
The 401 always reaches the caller; the adopt routes test stops flaking on Windows. Could break: nothing, if the drain is bounded by the body cap.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused request's reply always arrives
Before: 1 failure in 9 scoped-suite runs this round; 0 in 3 isolated runs
After: 0 failures in N repeated runs
Method: experiment - the scoped suite was re-run; the failure is load-dependent, so it needs a loop to measure
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tests/adopt/test_routes.py:55-57 live.request('/adopt', method='POST', body={}, token=None)
E ConnectionAbortedError: [WinError 10053] (tests/adopt/conftest.py:345 connection.getresponse())
src/athena/daemon/server.py:809, :939 self._fail(error(401, 'foreign_token', ...)) before the body is read
instrument: loop the POST-without-token request 200 times against a live daemon on Windows and count ConnectionAbortedError (control red: >0 today under load); out-of-scope seam: daemon-service (src/athena/daemon/server.py)

title: An every-N-days chore set without a start counts from the UTC date, not hers
body:
## Summary
A cadence rule `every_days` posted with no `start` begins N days after today's UTC date, while every other date the chores code computes (the suggestion, the upcoming list) is in the person's own zone, so near midnight the first occurrence lands a day early or late.

## Description
cadence.rule_from (src/athena/adopt/cadence.py:196-198) fills a missing start from `today or datetime.now(UTC).date()`; case_route (src/athena/adopt/chores.py:587) calls it with no `today` before the zone is known, then set_cadence computes next_run_at in the person's zone (chores.py:298-299). _cadence_reply's suggestion uses `now.astimezone(tz).date()` (chores.py:551-553). For a person in UTC-7 setting 'every 30 days' at 20:00 local (03:00 UTC next day) the start is 31 local days away; in UTC+10 at 08:00 local it is 29. Fixed looks like: resolve the zone first and pass rule_from the local date.

## Flow
- POST /adopt/cases/<proj>/cadence {rule: {kind: every_days, every_days: 30}, timezone: 'America/Denver'} at 20:00 local
- rule_from fills start = UTC tomorrow + 30
- next_run_at is the first local 09:00 on or after that start: one day later than she asked

## Expected impact
A chore set late in her evening comes due the day she expects. Measured by start vs local today + N at two clock times. Could break: nothing stored (start is written once, at set).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - start = her local today + N
Before: walked: UTC-7 at 20:00 local -> start is local today + 31
After: local today + 30 at every hour
Method: simulation - walked two zones; a clocked test needs the route to take a clock for rule_from, which is the fix's own seam
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/adopt/cadence.py:197 start = ((today or datetime.now(UTC).date()) + timedelta(days=every)).isoformat()
src/athena/adopt/chores.py:587 rule = cad.rule_from(body['rule']) ...  (no today, zone not yet read)
src/athena/adopt/chores.py:551-553 suggest_for_case(..., now.astimezone(tz).date())
instrument: tests/adopt/test_chores.py: set_cadence via case_route with a fake clock at 03:00 UTC and timezone 'Test/Euro' or a UTC-7 fixture zone; assert rule.start == local date + N (control red today)

title: A case file's receipts list grows without bound and is rewritten whole on every write
body:
## Summary
Every 'done' appends a full receipt (up to 20 cards with 6 params each, 10 notes) to the case file's JSON block, and nothing ever trims it; each later approval, done or space change rewrites the whole file.

## Description
CaseBook.append_receipt (src/athena/adopt/cases.py:456-478) appends to `extra['receipts']` and rewrites goals/<proj>.md through write_goal; save() and set_space() carry the list forward (_extra, cases.py:507-516). render_case also prints one 'Your runs' line per receipt into the markdown (cases.py:164-167). GET /adopt/cases/<proj>/runs reads all of them to answer 20 (routes.py:261-268), and the chores loop's review reads the file per case per call. A weekly chore is ~52 receipts a year, each up to a few KB: the file a person is meant to read becomes mostly JSON, and every write costs the whole history. Deciding a cap means deciding what is kept (archive to a sibling file, or drop the oldest) - dropping is irreversible, so this is the owner's call.

## Flow
- a weekly chore pressed done for a year -> 52 receipts in the block and 52 lines in 'Your runs'
- each approve / done / space move rewrites all of it
- proposal: keep the latest N in the case file and move older receipts to goals/<proj>.runs.md (append-only), or cap with an announced '(showing N of M)'

## Expected impact
The case file stays readable and its writes stay small; the history is kept where the owner decides. Measured by file bytes after 52 dones. Could break: run_started() reads only the last receipt, so it is safe; anything reading all receipts would see fewer.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - a bounded case file
Before: walked: 52 receipts x ~3 KB (20 cards x 6 params at 120 chars) -> ~150 KB of block in one goal file, rewritten on each write
After: a bounded block (N latest) plus an append-only archive
Method: simulation - sizes computed from the caps in receipts.py; the policy (archive vs drop) is not the sweep's to choose
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
src/athena/adopt/cases.py:470 extra['receipts'] = [*(held ...), runs.as_dict(receipt)]  (no cap)
src/athena/adopt/cases.py:164-167 one 'Your runs' line per stored receipt
src/athena/adopt/receipts.py:71-77 CARDS_CAP 20, NOTES_CAP 10, PARAMS_CAP 6, PARAM_TEXT_CAP 120
